query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating machine learning–trained interatomic potentials with high-throughput CALPHAD and advanced molecular dynamics simulations will enable accurate and efficient determination of melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and key liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across single‐phase high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Pristine, chemically disordered high-entropy alloys (e.g., equiatomic BCC or FCC structures) in the solid state.
generation.intervention: Apply an integrated computational framework that combines ML-trained interatomic potentials (for precise energy landscape description) with CALPHAD thermodynamic databases and high-fidelity MD/Monte Carlo simulations to sample the phase transition region.
generation.conditions: Simulations conducted under controlled thermal conditions spanning from below the melting point to above the liquid phase, focusing on HEAs with moderate compositional complexity and single-phase stability.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions and short-range chemical order that influence atomic vibrations and the free energy landscape near melting.
generation.mechanism: ML-trained potentials capture subtle interaction effects and local lattice distortions in multi-component systems, while CALPHAD integration ensures consistency with macroscopic thermodynamics. This combination facilitates efficient sampling of atomic configurations near melting, enabling the extraction of melting temperature, fusion enthalpy/entropy, and volume changes alongside key liquid-phase properties by analyzing atomic displacement, energy fluctuations, and phase transition dynamics.
generation.predicted_outcome: Predicted melting temperatures and fusion thermodynamic properties with an accuracy within approximately ±5–10% of experimental values, along with a quantitative description of liquid-phase behavior over a wide compositional range of single-phase HEAs.
generation.baseline: Traditional ab initio or classical MD simulations lacking ML enhancement or CALPHAD integration, which typically suffer from limited configurational sampling and higher computational cost, leading to less accurate or less efficient predictions.
generation.boundary: The approach is expected to be most applicable to single-phase HEAs with moderate compositional complexity; systems that exhibit strong phase separation, ordering, or multi-phase behavior may lie outside the reliable prediction range.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative performance in systems with pronounced short-range ordering or extreme compositional heterogeneity remains uncertain and requires further experimental validation. The exact error margins may vary depending on the quality of the ML potential and the availability of comprehensive CALPHAD data.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a set of well-characterized single-phase HEAs and computationally predict their melting temperature, fusion enthalpy/entropy, volume change at melting, and select liquid-phase properties using the integrated ML+CALPHAD/MD framework. Perform corresponding experimental measurements using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), high-temperature X-ray or neutron diffraction, and complementary thermophysical measurements. Compare the computational predictions with experimental data.
measurements: Volume change at melting (via high-temperature diffraction)
Liquid-phase properties such as viscosity or thermal conductivity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted values deviate by more than 5–10% on average from the experimental measurements across a statistically significant number of HEA compositions, then the proposed integrated approach is considered falsified.

System: Equiatomic bcc HfNbTaTiZr (HEA). Processing: Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations combined with Monte Carlo (MC) Kawasaki exchange process; samples evolved from random to SRO over up to 4.7 million MC steps at 300 K.. System: Quaternary W-Ta-V-Cr high-entropy alloy with atomic composition 38% W, 36% Ta, 15% Cr, and 11% V.
